author: Worldview Sorter AI editorial review
currentBehavior: The Quick-route public-testability rule has an exact proposition and direct evidence, but no rule-linked supporting academic claim.
proposedBehavior: Pin one narrow scholarly claim to the existing public-testability rule. Do not change questions, answer directions, thresholds, or affinity doctrine.
rationale: Reviewed both item wordings and the SEP discussion. Public explanations can trace the conceptual basis while retaining explicit non-entailments and neighboring false positives.

philosophicalBasis.proposition: Public repeatable testing merits greater confidence than a comparably unsupported private method.
nonEntailments: Public testing is infallible or the only possible source of knowledge.
Private experience has no personal evidential value.
philosophicalBasis.existingGap: Quick had zero rule-linked supporting source claims despite 30 direct interpretation opportunities.
philosophicalBasis.scholarlyDisagreement: Philosophers dispute the theory-ladenness and evidential role of observation. The claim is restricted to the comparison actually asked.

sourceClaims.claim: Intersubjectively ascertainable observations and public theory testing are a recognized rationale for the epistemic credibility of empirical claims; the account also acknowledges theory-ladenness and does not make every private experience worthless.
